inputs.original_text: John Lahart of Fianna Fáil is pushing to change inheritance-tax exemptions, calling the current system “wholly unfair” to people without children. And he’s not speaking in isolation: party colleagues have recently made similar calls to review how inheritance tax treats different family structures. They’re presenting this as fairness, but the coordinated push looks like an effort to steer the rules around who gets to keep or inherit wealth. The public justification is only part of the story.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart of Fianna Fáil is pushing to change inheritance-tax exemptions, and his colleagues have been making similar calls. They’re selling it as fairness for people without children, but the coordinated timing suggests a deeper effort to reshape who can keep or inherit wealth. “Fairness” may just be the cover story; the real question is whose interests these changes would serve.
